queries.hook: A fire lit by seeing what others achieved; the resolve to rise, gather your strength and take on what is yours to do.
queries.diagnose: Resolve fades when the mind runs ahead to the prize or looks sideways at others; it holds when the work itself is the reward.

hook.speaker: Bhartrihari
hook.setting: From 'Worship of Shiva': gratitude for a simple life.
hook.sanskrit: यदेतत्स्वच्छन्दं विहरणमकार्पण्यमशनं सहार्यैः संवासः श्रुतमुपशमैकव्रतफलम् । मनो मन्दस्पन्दं बहिरपि चिरस्यापि विमृशन् न जाने कस्यैष परिणतिरुदारस्य तपसः ॥
hook.line: Freedom, simple food, good company, learning that brings calm: what did I do to deserve this?
hook.translation: This freedom to wander at will, food eaten without humiliation, living among noble people, learning whose only fruit is calm, a mind that stirs only gently even when it looks outward for long: I do not know what generous austerity this is the fruit of.
hook.why: Gratitude for a simple life, and devotion without rivalry between forms of God.

alternates.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
alternates.setting: Letter from Alameda, California, 18 April 1900, after laying down his role as leader.
alternates.line: I am glad I was born, glad I suffered so, glad I did make big blunders, glad to enter peace.
alternates.translation: I am glad I was born, glad I suffered so, glad I did make big blunders, glad to enter peace.
alternates.why: Honest looking back, with gratitude for the mistakes, can bring peace.

prasang.title: 'I am drifting': a letter from Alameda (1900)
prasang.summary: Two years before his death, worn out, he writes that he has laid down the role of leader. He is glad he was born, glad he suffered, glad he made big blunders. He admits that ambition, personality, fear and love of power lay behind his work, and says they are fading as he drifts toward peace.
prasang.lesson: Honest looking back, with gratitude for the mistakes, can bring peace.

alternates.speaker: Bhishma
alternates.setting: Yudhishthira asks Bhishma how an eldest brother should treat his younger brothers, and they him.
alternates.sanskrit: दशाचार्यानुपाध्याय उपाध्यायान्पिता दश / दश चैव पितॄन्माता सर्वां वा पृथिवीमपि / गौरवेणाभिभवति नास्ति मातृसमो गुरुः
alternates.line: There is no teacher like a mother.
alternates.translation: A teacher outweighs ten instructors, a father ten teachers, and a mother ten fathers, even the whole earth. There is no teacher equal to a mother.
alternates.why: Overlook small faults, correct gently, share fairly, and don't let outsiders divide you.

prasang.title: Bhishma on elder and younger siblings
prasang.summary: Yudhishthira asks how the eldest brother should treat the younger ones. Bhishma: overlook small faults and correct gently, beware outsiders who sow division, divide property equally, and honour the mother above all.
prasang.lesson: Overlook small faults, correct gently, share fairly, and don't let outsiders divide you.

verse.for_you: You feel the nation turning, and your family is well. This freedom to move and learn, shared with good people, is its own reward.
verse.try_today: Notice one small thing today that lets your mind rest without reaching for more.
verse.scene_line: You sit with good company, eating simply, learning, while your mind looks outward without stirring.

verse.speaker: Sanatkumara
verse.setting: The next step: action rests on happiness.
verse.sanskrit: यदा वै सुखं लभतेऽथ करोति नासुखं लब्ध्वा करोति सुखमेव लब्ध्वा करोति सुखं त्वेव विजिज्ञासितव्यमिति सुखं भगवो विजिज्ञास इति ॥
verse.line: We act only when we find joy in it. Understand the joy, and action follows.
verse.translation: When one finds happiness, one acts. No one acts without finding happiness; only by finding happiness does one act. So happiness itself must be understood. 'Sir, I wish to understand happiness.'
verse.why: Success and learning don't cure sadness; only the infinite does.

prasang.title: Narada: learned but sad
prasang.summary: Narada, who has mastered every science of his day, comes to Sanatkumara and admits he is unhappy: he knows words, not himself. Sanatkumara leads him step by step from names up through action and joy to the infinite, teaching that happiness is found only in the vast, never in the small.
prasang.story_hook: Narada knew every subject worth knowing, and still came to Sanatkumara feeling sad.
prasang.lesson: Success and learning don't cure sadness; only the infinite does.

why: Narada: learned and still grieving (Chandogya Upanishad 7.1.3)

verse.speaker: Vidura
verse.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
verse.sanskrit: न हृष्यत्यात्मसंमाने नावमानेन तप्यते / गाङ्गो ह्रद इवाक्षोभ्यो यः स पण्डित उच्यते
verse.line: Don't swell with praise or burn at a slight; stay deep and still like a river pool.
verse.translation: One who is not elated when honoured, nor pained when slighted, and who stays unruffled like a deep pool of the Ganga, is called wise.
verse.why: Decide calmly, act steadily, forgive freely, and know what real happiness is made of.

prasang.title: Vidura Niti: the wise and the fool
prasang.summary: Sleepless before the peace talks, King Dhritarashtra calls his half-brother Vidura for counsel. Vidura describes the marks of the wise and the fool, the faults that block progress, and the six joys of life.
prasang.lesson: Decide calmly, act steadily, forgive freely, and know what real happiness is made of.

verse.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
verse.setting: Karma-Yoga classes, New York, winter 1895–96, chapter 1: how work shapes character.
verse.line: Watch a man do his most common actions; those are indeed the things which will tell you the real character of a great man.
verse.translation: If you really want to judge of the character of a man, look not at his great performances. Every fool may become a hero at one time or another. Watch a man do his most common actions; those are indeed the things which will tell you the real character of a great man. Great occasions rouse even the lowest of human beings to some kind of greatness, but he alone is the really great man whose character is great always, the same wherever he be.
verse.why: Character is built in ordinary actions, and you are building it right now.

prasang.title: Karma-Yoga 1: how work makes character
prasang.summary: He defines karma as work and says character is the sum of the impressions our actions leave. Misery teaches as much as joy, and character shows in small daily actions, not big moments. The ideal worker finds calm in the middle of intense activity.
prasang.lesson: Character is built in ordinary actions, and you are building it right now.

why: one big success proves little about who one is

verse.speaker: Teacher
verse.setting: The most quoted lines of the graduation address.
verse.sanskrit: देवपितृकार्याभ्यां न प्रमदितव्यम् । मातृदेवो भव । पितृदेवो भव । आचार्यदेवो भव । अतिथिदेवो भव ।
verse.line: Treat your mother as divine, your father as divine, your teacher as divine, your guest as divine.
verse.translation: Do not neglect your duties to the gods and the ancestors. Let your mother be a god to you. Let your father be a god to you. Let your teacher be a god to you. Let your guest be a god to you.
verse.why: Truth, right action, gratitude and graceful giving: a whole life in one speech.
verse.misuse: Honouring parents does not mean accepting mistreatment or giving up your own conscience.

prasang.title: The graduation address
prasang.summary: As a student finishes his studies and leaves to start family life, the teacher gives him parting instructions: speak truth, do right, keep learning, honour mother, father, teacher and guest, give with grace. He even tells the student to copy only the teachers' good conduct, and when in doubt to act as thoughtful, gentle people would.
prasang.lesson: Truth, right action, gratitude and graceful giving: a whole life in one speech.

verse.for_you: You see the good direction your family is in, and you want to keep it going. Let the care you give them be as natural as the gratitude you feel. This is how you honour the life you share.
verse.try_today: Offer one small act of care to someone you live with today.
verse.scene_line: You see your family in good health and you wish to keep it that way.

why: those who raised and taught you are to be honoured as one honours a deity
the guest and the elder are served as sacred

verse.speaker: Vidula
verse.setting: Queen Vidula rouses her son Sanjaya, who lies defeated and despairing after losing his kingdom.
verse.sanskrit: नैव राज्ञा दरः कार्यो जातु कस्यांचिदापदि / अथ चेदपि दीर्णः स्यान्नैव वर्तेत दीर्णवत्
verse.line: In a crisis, you may be shaken inside. Don't let fear make your decisions for you.
verse.translation: A leader should never show fear in any crisis. Even if shaken inside, he should not act like a shaken man.
verse.why: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.
verse.misuse: This is about not acting from panic, not about hiding your feelings from everyone.

prasang.title: Vidula rouses her defeated son
prasang.summary: Kunti sends Yudhishthira the old story of Queen Vidula, who finds her son lying defeated after losing his kingdom. She shames, then reasons, then encourages him until he rises and fights for it again.
prasang.story_hook: A prince lay in bed after losing everything, until his mother walked in and refused to let him stay there.
prasang.lesson: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.

why: Courage and steadiness are the wheels of the chariot that wins; do not let fear decide.
Composure for those who depend on one

story.title: Ram cannot repay Hanuman
story.story_hook: Hanuman had burned a city and found the queen; now he lay on the ground in front of Ram and refused to stand up.
story.summary: Back from Lanka, Hanuman tells Ram how Sita survives: his name guards her day and night. Ram, in tears, asks whether one who relies on him can meet calamity; Hanuman answers that the only calamity is forgetting him. Ram says he can never repay Hanuman and cannot even look him in the face; Hanuman falls at his feet and will not get up. Offered anything, he asks only for unwavering devotion, and credits every deed to Ram.
story.lesson: Do the work, give away the credit, and ask only to keep loving.
story.hook_title: Hanuman lay at Ram's feet and refused to stand up
story.teaser: Hanuman lay at Ram's feet and refused to stand up
